content: The preparation of samples for analysis of water-dispersible granules (WG) should follow the method outlined in CIPAC MT 166, titled Sample preparation for analytical determination of WG. Samples for testing and analysis should ideally be taken from freshly opened commercial containers to ensure integrity and accuracy. The properties specified in the guidelines are critical for ensuring optimal field performance. These properties include water dispersibility, dustiness, flow characteristics, and resistance to attrition. When drafting specifications, clauses should not be omitted, additional clauses should not be inserted, and limits should not be relaxed beyond those provided in the guidelines without consulting Section 4. Only applicable notes from the guideline's end should be incorporated into the specific specification. WG formulations must be in the form of granules, contained within sealed water-soluble bags, and designed for application after disintegration and dispersion in water. The formulation should be dry, free-flowing, nearly dust-free or essentially non-dusty, and free from visible extraneous matter or hard lumps. Identity tests for the active ingredient must be conducted, and if the identity remains uncertain, at least one additional test must be performed. The active ingredient content should meet the specified limits, calculated as H2SO4 or NaOH, depending on the test. Suspensibility tests should be performed on a suspension containing the WG and the bag material in the actual application ratio, prepared according to the procedure described in the guidelines. A minimum percentage of the formulation should remain in suspension after 30 minutes in CIPAC Standard Water D at 30 ± 2°C. Persistent foam tests should also be conducted on a suspension containing the WG and the bag material, prepared as per the guidelines. The maximum foam volume after one minute should not exceed the specified limit. Dustiness should be evaluated using either the gravimetric or optical method. The formulation should have a maximum collected dust of 30 mg (gravimetric method) or a maximum dust factor of 25 (optical method). Attrition resistance and particle size distribution should also be assessed, ensuring that a specified percentage of the formulation passes through a 5 mm test sieve after 20 drops. The dissolution of the bag should be tested using a sample of the emptied and cleaned bag, along with an appropriate proportion of the WG, in CIPAC Standard Water D. The flow time of the suspension should not exceed the specified limit. Packaging should be watertight and capable of withstanding storage at 54°C for 14 days without leakage or rupture. Bags should be tested for integrity before and after storage to ensure no signs of damage during normal handling. Water-dispersible tablets (WT) are pre-formed solids of uniform shape and size, intended for application after disintegration and dispersion in water using conventional spraying equipment. The formulation should consist of unbroken, free-flowing tablets, free from visible extraneous matter. Identity tests for WT should confirm the active ingredient, with additional tests conducted if necessary. Disintegration time for effervescent tablets should not exceed the specified maximum. Wet sieve tests should ensure that a maximum percentage of the formulation is retained on a 75 µm test sieve. Suspensibility tests should confirm that a minimum percentage of the formulation remains in suspension after 30 minutes in CIPAC Standard Water D at 30 ± 2°C. Effervescent tablets should incorporate an effervescent system, and their disintegration should be complete before conducting CIPAC tests. Storage stability tests should be performed on intact tablets, and the mass of the sample used in tests should be specified at the highest recommended rate. Water-emulsifiable granules (EG) are formulations designed to form oil-in-water emulsions upon disintegration and dissolution in water. They consist of granules containing active ingredients solubilized or diluted in an organic solvent, absorbed in a water-soluble polymeric shell or matrix. The formulation should be homogeneous, dry, free-flowing, and free from visible extraneous matter or hard lumps. Upon dilution in water, the granules should provide a stable emulsion. Identity tests for EG should confirm the active ingredient, with additional tests conducted if necessary. The formulation should meet specified limits for active ingredient content, particle size distribution, and attrition resistance. The material should pass through a 5 mm test sieve after 20 drops, and the maximum foam volume after one minute should not exceed the specified limit. Water-emulsifiable powders (EP) are applied as oil-in-water emulsions after dispersion in water. They contain active ingredients solubilized or diluted in organic solvents, absorbed in a water-soluble polymer powder or matrix. The formulation should be homogeneous, dry, free-flowing, and free from visible extraneous matter or hard lumps. Upon dilution in water, the powders should disperse and emulsify effectively. For all formulations, methods of analysis for active ingredients and relevant impurities must be CIPAC, AOAC, or equivalent. If unpublished methods are used, full details and validation data must be submitted to FAO/WHO.
